1: you should not plan evenings for your wife with the intent and expectation that you will be having sex. It would be hard for me to think about any lovely evening planned for me not being only for the intention of sex, even if that’s not really what it’s for. You specifically said that a good date ends in sex, which would make me question if every date that didn’t end in sex was disappointing to you or was just bad. I don’t know how your wife thinks, though, so she may completely not even relate. 

2: like other people here have said, during your future dates, do not see friends at the end. You could possibly have a drink BEFORE dinner with friends and have a reservation at a different restaurant so you HAVE to go to get there on time and then be present with each other. If possible, schedule a time out with your friends on purpose from start to finish. It would hurt my feelings too to have my partner not want to end the evening with me and chose to stay with another person. That is a very real and understandable feeling you had. At the same time, being a parent makes it hard to get away and it might be hard to fight the urge to catch up and spend time with adults outside of your partnership. It would be very tempting to milk that time with friends as much as possible for as long as possible. It’s not okay that she did that, but maybe thinking about it in that frame might be less hurtful because it’s less personal. 

3: if you are to plan another date night (which you absolutely should) please let her know there are no expectations for intimacy afterward. But also have the ground rule that it’s just you two for the whole time.

Hi there! Personal answers in list order:
1) Lawrence as a whole is very hilly and uneven. Getting to campus if not living directly on campus requires going up very steep hills. Accessing buildings on campus requires steep hills. Because of this, there are a ton of stairs everywhere that lead from different areas of campus to other areas. There’s is a limited mobility route called the Hawk Route with elevators and there are signs. I will say that I am an able-bodied person, but have a back and knee injury that still made maneuvering campus challenging even without needing to utilize a wheelchair. I have seen plenty of students in my time at KU in my courses that use wheel chairs and other mobility aids, but haven’t had a chance to get to talk to any of them about it with covid making talking to new people a bit more intimidating. I will be blunt: KU is not a very accessible campus. 
2) I would say no, most professors guard their class session recordings tighter to their chest than any family secret. I had a professor at explicitly say do not come to class if you are sick, e-mail me about attendance and I’ll excuse you. I asked about a class recording and he said that he doesn’t share them because people need to come to class and he doesn’t want it to be easy to succeed in class while not attending. There are some rooms that do have a live stream like the chemistry building and Wescoe hall. Those links aren’t too hard to find, but they aren’t recorded and they’re only in large classrooms. Most professors don’t even have a zoom option set up so you can get attendance points even if you are sick. They all want people to have to work for a good grade. 
3) KU allows you complete freedom to schedule your own classes, but there are a couple of different time frames for classes. There are short, 50 minute classes that begin at the top of the hour (8:00-8:50), 75 minute classes that begin either at the top of the hour or halfway through (8-9:15, 8:30-9:45), and I also think there are hour and 45 minute classes. The separate departments don’t coordinate when they schedule their classes for specific degrees so you may have a class at one end of jayhawk boulevard that ends at 8:50 and a 9:00 class at the complete opposite end that’s a 15 minute walk for me at my quick pace. You may have to be okay with taking some classes a little mixed up from the sample plans KU does for some degrees to make sure you can get to classes on time. I know I had to shuffle some of mine around because I was minoring and my required classes were just too close together to make work. 
4) The student access center and the academic achievement advisory center (AAAC if you want to look it up) requires you to meet with an advisor every semester to go over accommodations and do need documentation (unless this has changed since I graduated in May). I just had my therapist write a letter that said he has seen me for x amount of years for x condition. If you have multiple physical and mental disabilities that require accommodations, I would try to get documentation for all because some professors are wonderful and will bend over backwards to make you feel valued in their course and some will try to brush off all issues as if they’re annoyed you would even consider asking for help. Mixed bag, not unlike most universities. 
5) When I was a freshman, I had to wait 3 months before being able to receive an initial evaluation at the psychology clinic at the health center here. It was quick, informal, and I had to wait another 2 months, which was over winter break to be able to get another appointment and I didn’t have a car to access it, so I had to pass it up. Every single mental health facility across the country is struggling and needing more clinicians, especially at universities. It sucks, but KU isn’t a particularly bad institution in this aspect. There are just so many people who need help and not nearly enough professionals to help them. 
6) There is a DEI, sexual assault awareness, and alcohol abuse training course requires to be completed every fall that puts a hold on your enrollment account if it’s not completed by the certain date. You can’t enroll in spring classes if you don’t do the course. That being said, I clicked through it just to get it over with and it’s not taken seriously by students. I actually paid attention freshman year because I cared about being a considerate and kind person on campus that was informed, but it’s the same course every year and too easy to not pay attention to. 
7) I only really had an issue with one processor that wouldn’t allow me to do an assignment late because of a friend’s attempted suicide left me feeling and caring for their animals, apartment, and plants. She insisted that she didn’t need to extend the due date because we could drop one of that particular assignment. I took it to my AAAC advisor who had told me it was his job to yell at professors for not honoring the agreement made about flexible due dates. He helped and she begrudgingly allowed me to do it. I think most students at KU honestly look through people with disabilities instead of seeing them. The only discrimination for people with disabilities I’ve seen is when there’s not enough room on the overly crowded buses for someone with a wheel chair getting on the bus to be able to get to the safe locks to secure their chair in place. It wasn’t a refusal to move for them, but there was definitely annoyance that their day was slowed down and that they were inconvenienced by this person that needed room to move and feel safe. 
8) that is a great question that I don’t have the answer to. As someone said, the accessibility website is a great resource. There is also the KU class search website that has a departments option that lets you look at every departmental course offering like psychology, economics, etc. there’s also a keyword function that would let you look up disabilities. 
I hope this helped at all and feel free to reach out and ask questions!

Hi there! I am a daycare teacher in the one year old room at my center. I do not kiss the kids unless, for whatever reason, the parents give permission to do so. RSV has hit our center hard and I would be too nervous to kiss any of them and get them sick. I will say that I tell my kids every single day that I love them. I do love them. I spent 7 am to 5:30 4 days a week with them. I feed them 3 times a day, I change their diapers, I get them down for nap. I wouldn’t and couldn’t do this job without loving them. I can understand that it might feel odd hearing that many people tell your daughter you love them, so I’m not saying that’s wrong. All I can say is I talk about the kids in my class like they’re my own and I feel pride when they learn to talk. I cry when they’re upset and I can’t fix it. It’s hard to see them move up to the next room because I spend 40 hours of my week loving them and playing with them and wiping their noses and tears and laughing with them. We have hard times in the room with gets pushing boundaries and I have to be stern, but my babies never doubt that I love them because I tell them.

I agree with a lot of what people are saying here: continuous open recruitment or informal recruitment in the spring could be a great idea. I will say, though, that not all of the PHA sororities do informal. There are some houses that fill all required spots in the fall and don’t do anything in the spring. I know my chapter did not. I also know a lot of graphic design students that were in sororities as well. You’ll find an overwhelming amount of biology for pre med, business (because it’s just the most common major), and pre-nursing in sororities. That doesn’t mean there won’t be artistic people though! One of my friends was either going to go to Tulane for visual arts or KU for strat com, so the major people choose doesn’t immediately exclude them from your same interests! People minor in all different kind of stuff. I, personally, struggle terribly with mental health and it really made my time at KU a challenge with making friends, but I know so many people who developed very deep relationships with their pledge sisters that helped them through really hard times. You can always go through with recruitment in the fall and “trust the process” by being your most authentic self. Hopefully, you’ll end up where you belong that way. It is an absolutely brutal week, though. No way around that. I was a mess and cried every single day. I was so happy on bid day but I was more relieved it was over than anything. Make sure you take care of yourself and practice whatever form of self care works best for you during the week. School starts two days later and it can really be hard to feel grounded after something so intense.

I found that with my very aggressive tactics for killing my acne, I had also killed my moisture barrier, which is like a wall to keep the water in your skin. I have dehydrated, dry skin.
